flags.why: The Northern tag excludes ordinary Central Vietnamese usage, including official usage in Quảng Nam ([source](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/toan-van-quy-hoach-tinh-quang-nam-thoi-ky-2021-2030-tam-nhin-den-nam-2050-119240118185302026.htm)).
The example needs nói láo to express lying; láo với mẹ alone means being insolent toward one's mother.
flags.fix: Nó nói láo với mẹ rằng nó đã đi học. = He lied to his mother, saying he'd gone to school.

flags.why: The title refers to someone holding the rank of prince and is not restricted to a ruler's brother ([source](https://www.vjol.info/vuong-gia-la-gi)).
flags.fix: prince (a man holding the title vương)

flags.why: Calling a people man rợ is derogatory, as the example itself illustrates.
The entry omits the everyday literal meaning of becoming ill.
flags.fix: to get sick; to fall ill

flags.why: Trật meaning incorrect or wrong is chiefly Southern usage.
Sen as a term for a maidservant is disparaging, especially in con sen.
The example defines intuition instead of showing the word in use.
flags.fix: Tôi làm theo trực giác của mình. = I followed my intuition.

flags.why: Quấy meaning morally wrong is characteristic of Southern usage ([source](https://www.tapchisonglam.vn/van-vuong-voi-phuong-ngu/)).
